spots.name: Millennium of Russia
spots.summary: The Millennium of Russia is a bronze monument in the Novgorod Kremlin. It was erected in 1862 to celebrate the millennium of Rurik's arrival to Novgorod, an event traditionally taken as a starting point of the history of Russian statehood.

spots.name: Saint Sophia Cathedral
spots.summary: The Cathedral of Saint Sophia, the Holy Wisdom of God, in Veliky Novgorod, Russia, is the cathedral church of the Metropolitan of Novgorod and the mother church of the Novgorodian Eparchy.

spots.name: Novgorod Detinets
spots.summary: The Novgorod Detinets, also known as the Novgorod Kremlin, is a fortified complex (detinets) in Veliky Novgorod, Russia. It stands on the left bank of the Volkhov River about two miles north of where it empties out of Lake Ilmen.

spots.name: Yuriev Monastery

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The St. George's (Yuriev) Monastery is usually cited as Russia's oldest monastery. It stands in 5 kilometers south of Novgorod on the left bank of the Volkhov River near where it flows out of Lake Ilmen. The monastery used to be the most important in the medieval Novgorod Republic.

spots.name: Church of the Transfiguration on Ilyina Street

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of the Transfiguration of the Savior is a former Russian Orthodox Church that stands on Ilyina (Elijah) Street in Veliky Novgorod just east of the Marketplace. The current building was built in 1374 and frescoed by Theophanes the Greek in 1378.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of the Transfiguration on Ilyina Street

spots.name: Historic Monuments of Novgorod and Surroundings
spots.summary: The Historic Monuments of Novgorod and Surroundings is a composite World Heritage Site which includes a number of medieval monuments in and around Veliky Novgorod, Russia. The site was inscribed in 1992.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Historic Monuments of Novgorod and Surroundings

spots.name: Yaroslav's Court
spots.summary: Yaroslav's Court was a princely compound in the city of Veliky Novgorod, Russia. It is now roughly the area around the Trade Side and includes the following buildings: St. Nicholas Cathedral, the Church of St. Procopius, and the Church of the Myrrh-Bearing Women.

spots.summary: The Saviour Church on Nereditsa Hill near Novgorod is a 12th-century Orthodox church dedicated to the feast of the Saviour's Transfiguration.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint Nicholas Cathedral, founded by Mstislav the Great in 1113 and consecrated in 1136, is the oldest surviving building in the central part of Veliky Novgorod after the Saint Sophia Cathedral.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Church of St. Paraskevi in Veliky Novgorod is one of Russia's oldest churches, dating from 1207. The church is located at the city center, at the former Yaroslav's Court and the market square. It is currently a museum.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Transfiguration Church in Kovalyovo in Novgorodsky District, Novgorod Oblast, Russia, was built around 1345. The church was notable for the frescoes created in the 14th century. The church was destroyed to the ground during World War II and restored in 1970. Fragments of the frescoes have since been reconstructed.
